newsitem.title: JORDAN: Arafat in talks with King Hussein on new peace moves.
newsitem.headline: Arafat in talks with King Hussein on new peace moves.

text.p: Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat began talks in Amman on Sunday with King Hussein as Israeli and Palestinian negotiators met for the first time in more than two months, officials said.
They said King Hussein and Arafat began talks in Raghdan Palace immediately after the arrival of the Palestinian leader who flew from Gaza on board a Jordanian military helicopter.

Officials said Arafat would consult the king on the latest Egyptian moves to revive Israeli-Palestinian talks, in crisis since Israel broke ground three months ago on a Jewish settlement on an Arab East Jerusalem hill.
The two leaders would also review bilateral ties.
Israeli and Palestinian negotiators met on Sunday in Cairo after untangling a last-minute snag over Jewish settlements, part of the Egyptian diplomatic moves to help break the peace impasse.

Since a government headed by Prime Minister Abdul Salam al-Majali came to power last March, Jordan has pursued a more cautious role in Israeli-Palestinian peace moves, in contrast to Egypt which has replaced Washington as the main mediator, officials say.
